analyst_view.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday with Pio Esposito scoring a hat-trick; Calhanoglu (thigh, at least two weeks per Corriere dello Sport), Zielinski and Bonny are out and all three are now counted, while Bastoni is back from his European ban. Sky Sport Italia and L'Interista (citing Gazzetta) both expect Lautaro Martinez, short of rhythm after injury, to start on the bench with Thuram and Esposito up front; UEFA and Sports Mole still have him starting, so this is likely but not certain. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Jaquez and Sauer are out (counted) and Angelo Stiller has been cleared to travel and could even start (Bild via Bulinews), with Demirovic and Undav leading the line. French referee Francois Letexier (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already take Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny off Inter (about -16% together). What they don't know is that Lautaro, Inter's captain and best finisher, is expected on the bench by Sky and Gazzetta; with Esposito in form that is a mild cut, about 4%, to around 3.0. Stiller's possible return helps Stuttgart's build-up but is already how the numbers see them.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.1 corners, 6.2 of them Inter's, already up 6% for Inter's recent corner count. Dimarco and Spence or Diouf on the flanks and Stuttgart's wing-backs Leweling and Fuhrich keep the game wide, and losing Calhanoglu changes who takes the corners rather than how many, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.7 cards and already take a little off Inter for their quiet recent record and for referee Letexier, who sits near the average at 4.0 a game. There is no rivalry and no suspension angle, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.4 shots and already add about 20% to Inter's side for their recent shooting and take 7% off Stuttgart's. Inter at home with Esposito and Thuram should still shoot plenty, and Lautaro is expected to come on, so the volume should hold and I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, up 7% for Inter's accuracy lately and down 3% for Stuttgart's. With Lautaro, Inter's sharpest finisher, likely starting on the bench, which the numbers don't see, I take a small 3% off, to about 10.3.
